title: 2 Kings Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 6.

questions.question: Why did the sons of the prophets speak to Elisha at the beginning of the chapter?
options: They wanted to move because the place was too strait for them
They requested Elisha to heal a sick man
They asked for weapons to defend themselves
questions.correctAnswer: They wanted to move because the place was too strait for them
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:1 states the sons of the prophets said unto Elisha, 'Behold now, the place where we dwell with thee is too strait for us.'

questions.question: Where did the sons of the prophets want to go to get wood for building a new place to dwell?
questions.correctAnswer: Jordan
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:2 says they asked to go unto Jordan to take beams to make a place where they may dwell.

questions.question: How did Elisha respond when asked if he would go with the sons of the prophets to cut wood?
options: He asked them to wait for a better time
questions.correctAnswer: He said, 'I will go.'
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:3 records Elisha answering, 'I will go.'

questions.question: What happened to the axe head while they were cutting wood by the Jordan?
options: It got stuck in a tree
questions.correctAnswer: It fell into the water
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:5 states that while felling a beam, the axe head fell into the water.

questions.question: How did Elisha make the iron axe head float after it fell into the water?
options: He cut down a stick and cast it in the water
He prayed to the LORD to raise it
He threw a stone into the water
He used a rope to fish it out
questions.correctAnswer: He cut down a stick and cast it in the water
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:6 describes Elisha cutting down a stick and casting it into the water, causing the iron to swim.

questions.question: True or False: The iron axe head sank to the bottom and could not be retrieved.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: According to 2 Kings 6:7, Elisha told the man to take up the iron, and he put out his hand and took it.

questions.question: Who was warring against Israel according to 2 Kings 6?
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Syria
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:8 states that the king of Syria warred against Israel.

questions.question: What advice did the man of God send to the king of Israel regarding the Syrian army's movements?
options: Beware that thou pass not such a place
Hide your army in the mountains
questions.correctAnswer: Beware that thou pass not such a place
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:9 quotes the man of God warning the king of Israel to beware not to pass a certain place where the Syrians had come down.

questions.question: How many times did the king of Israel save himself by heeding the man of God's warning?
options: Many times, but the exact number is unknown
questions.correctAnswer: Not once nor twice
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:10 says the king saved himself there 'not once nor twice,' implying multiple times.

questions.question: True or False: The king of Syria was pleased that his plans were not being discovered.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:11 says the heart of the king of Syria was sore troubled by this, showing he was displeased.

questions.question: Who did the king of Syria suspect was revealing his plans to Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Elisha, the prophet in Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:12 records a servant telling the king that Elisha, the prophet in Israel, was telling the king of Israel the words he spoke in his bedchamber.

questions.question: True or False: The king of Syria sent an army to capture Elisha in Dothan.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:13-14 describe the king sending horses, chariots, and a great host to Dothan to capture Elisha.

questions.question: What was Elisha's response when his servant saw the army surrounding the city?
options: Fear not: for they that be with us are more
questions.correctAnswer: Fear not: for they that be with us are more
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:16 shows Elisha telling his servant not to fear because those with them were more than those with the enemy.

questions.question: In what city was Elisha when the Syrian army came to capture him?
questions.correctAnswer: Dothan
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:13 states that Elisha was in Dothan when the king of Syria planned to capture him.

questions.question: True or False: The sons of the prophets first asked Elisha to go with them to cut wood.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:2-3 show the sons of the prophets asked Elisha to let them go, and then one suggested he go with them; Elisha agreed, but they did not first ask him to go.

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 6:12, who was revealing the king of Syria's private words to the king of Israel?
options: A servant of the king of Israel
The king of Syria's own messenger
questions.correctAnswer: Elisha, the prophet in Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states that Elisha, the prophet in Israel, was telling the king of Israel the words spoken by the king of Syria in his bedchamber, revealing divine knowledge and God's protection over Israel.

questions.question: Where was Elisha when the king of Syria sent horses, chariots, and a great host to capture him?
questions.correctAnswer: Dothan
questions.explanation: Verse 13 and 14 reveal that Elisha was in Dothan when the Syrian king sent a great host to capture him, showing the strategic importance of this location in the conflict.

questions.question: What was Elisha's response when his servant was afraid upon seeing the enemy host encamp around the city?
options: Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them
questions.correctAnswer: Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them
questions.explanation: Verse 16 records Elisha's comforting words to his fearful servant, teaching trust in God's protection even when circumstances appear overwhelming.

questions.question: What did Elisha pray for to help his servant see the true reality of their situation?
options: LORD, open his eyes, that he may see
LORD, deliver us from our enemies
LORD, give us strength to fight
LORD, hide us from the Syrians
questions.correctAnswer: LORD, open his eyes, that he may see
questions.explanation: In verse 17, Elisha prays that the servant's spiritual eyes be opened, allowing him to see the heavenly horses and chariots of fire protecting them, emphasizing God's unseen power.

questions.question: How did Elisha handle the Syrian soldiers who came to capture him after their eyes were opened?
options: He prayed for them to be struck with blindness and then led them to Samaria
He fought them with his own hands
He called the Israelite army to attack
questions.correctAnswer: He prayed for them to be struck with blindness and then led them to Samaria
questions.explanation: Verses 18-19 explain that Elisha prayed for their blindness, then guided them to Samaria, showing mercy and divine control over the situation.

questions.question: What happened when Elisha prayed for the Syrian soldiers' eyes to be opened in Samaria?
options: They saw they were in the midst of Samaria
questions.correctAnswer: They saw they were in the midst of Samaria
questions.explanation: Verse 20 records that when Elisha prayed, their eyes were opened and they realized they were surrounded, demonstrating God's power and protection for Israel.

questions.question: How did Elisha instruct the king of Israel to treat the captured Syrian soldiers?
options: Set bread and water before them, and send them back to their master
Execute them to prevent future attacks
questions.correctAnswer: Set bread and water before them, and send them back to their master
questions.explanation: Verse 22 shows Elisha's instruction to treat captives with kindness and let them go, highlighting forgiveness and integrity in leadership.

questions.question: What was the result after the Syrian soldiers were fed and sent back to their master?
options: The bands of Syria came no more into the land of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The bands of Syria came no more into the land of Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 23 explains that this act of mercy resulted in peace, showing how generosity and trust in God can bring lasting protection.

questions.question: What does Elisha’s prayer for his servant’s eyes to be opened teach about faith in God during fearful situations?
options: Faith allows us to see beyond visible threats to God’s unseen protection
Faith requires us to ignore reality and hope for the best
Faith means we should fight our battles alone
Faith is unnecessary if we have a strong army
questions.correctAnswer: Faith allows us to see beyond visible threats to God’s unseen protection
questions.explanation: Verses 16-17 show that Elisha’s prayer enabled his servant to perceive the spiritual forces guarding them, teaching that faith helps believers trust God even when circumstances seem dire.

questions.question: What does Elisha’s refusal to harm the captive Syrians in verse 22 teach us about Christian virtues?
options: Forgiveness and compassion should guide how we treat our enemies
We should always seek revenge as a sign of strength
Captives must be punished to prevent future harm
Mercy is only for friends, not foes
questions.correctAnswer: Forgiveness and compassion should guide how we treat our enemies
questions.explanation: Verse 22 reveals Elisha’s command to treat captives kindly and not kill them, modeling humility, mercy, and integrity even towards adversaries.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 6:22-23 promise will happen if the king treats his captives with bread and water and sends them home?
options: The bands of Syria will come no more into the land of Israel
The captives will return with more soldiers
The captives will attack again immediately
questions.correctAnswer: The bands of Syria will come no more into the land of Israel
questions.explanation: Verses 22-23 link the act of mercy towards captives with the result that Syria’s bands cease invading Israel, showing the power of kindness and trust in God for peace.

questions.question: In 2 Kings 6:18, Elisha prayed for the enemy to be smitten with blindness. What does this teach about prayer and God’s protection?
options: Prayer can invoke God’s intervention to protect His people
Prayer has no effect on natural events
God only protects through armies, not prayer
Blindness was a punishment unrelated to prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer can invoke God’s intervention to protect His people
questions.explanation: Verse 18 shows Elisha’s prayer led to the Syrians being blinded, illustrating that prayer is a powerful means to seek God’s protection in trials.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Kings 6:16, Elisha told his servant to fear because the enemy's forces were greater than theirs.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 16 states the opposite: Elisha told his servant not to fear because those with them were more than those with the enemy, demonstrating trust in God's superior power.

questions.question: True or False: In 2 Kings 6:21, the king of Israel asked Elisha if he should strike the captured Syrians.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 21 records the king asking Elisha if he should smite the captives, indicating his initial inclination toward judgment before Elisha advised mercy.

questions.question: True or False: Elisha’s prayer in 2 Kings 6:17 resulted in the young man seeing a mountain filled with horses and chariots of fire surrounding Elisha.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 17 explicitly states God opened the servant's eyes and he saw the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisha, showing God’s supernatural protection.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 6.

questions.question: What was the king of Israel's reaction upon hearing the woman’s distressing story during the famine?
options: He ignored her and continued walking
He rent his clothes and wore sackcloth beneath his garments
He ordered a relief supply immediately
He laughed and dismissed her concerns
questions.correctAnswer: He rent his clothes and wore sackcloth beneath his garments
questions.explanation: Verse 2 Kings 6:30 states that when the king heard the woman's words, he rent his clothes and had sackcloth upon his flesh, which was a sign of mourning and distress.

questions.question: How did Elisha respond when the king of Israel asked if he should strike the captured Syrian soldiers?
options: He told the king to kill them all
He said not to strike them but to feed them and send them away
He encouraged the king to imprison them
He advised to ransom them for silver
questions.correctAnswer: He said not to strike them but to feed them and send them away
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:22 records Elisha advising the king not to smite the captives but to provide bread and water and send them back to their master.

questions.question: What was the result after Elisha fed and sent away the bands of Syria?
options: The Syrians attacked Israel more fiercely
The bands of Syria came no more into the land of Israel
The Syrians formed an alliance with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The bands of Syria came no more into the land of Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 2 Kings 6:23 states that after the Syrians were fed and sent away, they did not enter Israel's land again.

questions.question: What severe condition struck Samaria after Benhadad besieged it?
questions.correctAnswer: A great famine
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:25 describes a great famine during the siege of Samaria by Benhadad's forces.

questions.question: What does the extreme price of an ass's head and dove's dung during the siege symbolize in ancient Near Eastern culture?
questions.correctAnswer: Scarcity and desperation
questions.explanation: The exorbitant prices for normally cheap or worthless items like an ass's head and dove’s dung indicate extreme scarcity and desperation during the famine (2 Kings 6:25), reflecting a common ancient Near Eastern sign of severe famine conditions.

questions.question: In 2 Kings 6:31, the king says, 'God do so and more also to me, if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat shall stand on him this day.' What does this statement reveal about the king’s attitude towards Elisha?
options: He wants to honor Elisha publicly
He desires to have Elisha executed
He plans to make Elisha his advisor
questions.correctAnswer: He desires to have Elisha executed
questions.explanation: The king expresses a curse implying he wishes Elisha’s death, indicating hostility towards the prophet (2 Kings 6:31).

questions.question: How did Elisha prepare for the arrival of the king’s messenger sent to take his head?
options: He prayed for protection and hid
He instructed the elders to shut the door and seize the messenger
questions.correctAnswer: He instructed the elders to shut the door and seize the messenger
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:32 shows Elisha telling the elders to shut the door and hold the messenger fast when he arrives, indicating a strategic preparation.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word 'stranger' (רֵעַ, re'a) as it relates to the captives in 2 Kings 6:22, in the context of Israelite hospitality?
questions.correctAnswer: Neighbor or companion
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root word רֵעַ (re'a) traditionally means 'neighbor' or 'companion,' emphasizing the radical mercy Elisha advocates by treating captives as fellow human beings deserving care (2 Kings 6:22).

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of God’s unseen protection as demonstrated when Elisha's servant’s eyes were opened to see horses and chariots of fire?
questions.explanation: Psalm 91:11-12 speaks of God’s angels guarding His people, paralleling the invisible divine protection revealed to Elisha's servant (2 Kings 6:16-17).

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in 2 Kings 6:15-17, where the servant initially sees the enemy army but Elisha prays for his eyes to be opened to see the heavenly army?
questions.correctAnswer: Irony
questions.explanation: There is dramatic irony in the servant’s fear contrasted with the revelation of a greater unseen heavenly force protecting them (2 Kings 6:15-17).

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 6:33, what was Elisha’s perspective on the evil or calamity that had befallen Israel during the siege?
options: It was caused by enemy armies alone
It was a punishment from the LORD and inevitable
It was due to natural disaster
It was unrelated to divine will
questions.correctAnswer: It was a punishment from the LORD and inevitable
questions.explanation: Elisha states the evil is from the LORD and questions why he should wait further, indicating acceptance of divine judgment (2 Kings 6:33).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of mercy towards enemies as demonstrated by Elisha's treatment of the Syrian captives?
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: All these passages emphasize loving and showing mercy to enemies, paralleling Elisha’s mercy in 2 Kings 6:22-23.

questions.question: In the context of the siege described in 2 Kings 6, what does the king’s rhetorical question in verse 27 ('If the LORD do not help thee, whence shall I help thee?') imply about his faith and leadership?
options: He fully trusts in God’s help
He shows despair and acknowledges his own powerlessness
He blames his officials for the crisis
He is confident in military solutions
questions.correctAnswer: He shows despair and acknowledges his own powerlessness
questions.explanation: The king’s question reveals a sense of helplessness and dependence on divine intervention in the face of famine (2 Kings 6:27).

questions.question: True or False: The chapter 2 Kings 6 contains an example of typology where Elisha’s prayer for blinded enemies foreshadows Christ’s spiritual blindness on the cross.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Elisha's prayer in 2 Kings 6:18 for the enemy to be struck with blindness can be typologically seen as foreshadowing Christ’s spiritual blindness and rejection during His passion (see John 9:39-41).

questions.question: True or False: The chapter shows that the king of Syria was unaware of Elisha’s prophetic abilities until after the siege of Samaria.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:12 indicates that the king of Syria’s servants acknowledged Elisha’s role in revealing the king’s secrets well before the siege, showing awareness of his prophetic abilities.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's provision is illustrated when Elisha causes the iron axe head to float in the water?
options: God can perform miracles to provide for human needs
Man's ingenuity is sufficient without divine intervention
Natural resources are the primary means of God's provision
questions.correctAnswer: God can perform miracles to provide for human needs
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 6:6 shows Elisha's miraculous act of making the iron axe head float, demonstrating God's power to provide supernaturally. This aligns with biblical teaching on divine provision (Psalm 23:1; Philippians 4:19).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly revealed when Elisha prays for the young man's eyes to be opened and he sees the heavenly horses and chariots?
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipresence
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 6:17, God reveals the spiritual reality of heavenly forces surrounding Elisha, showing His omnipresence—His presence everywhere including the unseen spiritual realm (Psalm 139:7-10).

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 6:23 demonstrate a principle of sanctification in how the king of Israel treats the blinded Syrian soldiers?
options: By showing mercy, fostering peace and repentance
questions.correctAnswer: By showing mercy, fostering peace and repentance
questions.explanation: Verse 23 reveals that the king provided food and released the captives, reflecting sanctification as God’s people are called to mercy and peace (Romans 12:20).

questions.question: What combined theological insight about divine sovereignty and human conflict is taught by 2 Kings 6:11 and 2 Kings 6:33?
options: God sovereignly ordains trials and uses them for His purposes
Human plans always succeed without God's involvement
War is independent of divine will
God is uninvolved in earthly affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly ordains trials and uses them for His purposes
questions.explanation: Verses 11 and 33 show that despite Syrian opposition and threats to Elisha, the events are declared as 'evil of the LORD,' illustrating God's sovereign control over conflict (Isaiah 45:7).

questions.question: Which doctrine is exemplified by the king of Israel's refusal to kill the blinded Syrian soldiers and instead provide for them as captives?
options: The doctrine of mercy and forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of mercy and forgiveness
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 6:22, Elisha instructs the king to show kindness to captives, exemplifying divine mercy and forgiveness as key Christian doctrines (Ephesians 4:32).

questions.question: How does the narrative of the Syrian siege and famine in 2 Kings 6:24-25 contribute to the biblical theme of judgment and deliverance?
options: It illustrates God's judgment through famine and a call to repentance
It encourages reliance on political alliances only
It shows that suffering is unrelated to sin
It emphasizes human strength in warfare
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates God's judgment through famine and a call to repentance
questions.explanation: The siege causing famine (6:24-25) typifies divine judgment on Israel, calling for repentance as part of God's redemptive discipline (Deuteronomy 28:15-16).

questions.question: What does Elisha's prayer for blindness on the Syrian soldiers in 2 Kings 6:18 reveal about God's justice and mercy?
options: God executes justice but with mercy by not killing them immediately
God is indifferent to human sin
questions.correctAnswer: God executes justice but with mercy by not killing them immediately
questions.explanation: Verse 18 shows God’s justice in blinding the enemies but sparing their lives, allowing for repentance and mercy (Exodus 34:6-7).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine intervention in human conflicts is a myth and that 2 Kings 6:14-20 simply describes natural events. What does 2 Kings 6:14-20 actually teach about the spiritual realm's involvement in earthly battles?
options: The passage teaches that spiritual realities actively influence physical events
It confirms all events are purely natural with no spiritual dimension
It denies any supernatural involvement in history
It portrays spiritual beings as irrelevant
questions.correctAnswer: The passage teaches that spiritual realities actively influence physical events
questions.explanation: Verses 14-20 depict Elisha praying to reveal spiritual armies, demonstrating biblical teaching of unseen spiritual forces engaging in earthly affairs (Ephesians 6:12).

questions.question: What does the request of the sons of the prophets in 2 Kings 6:1-2 reveal about the importance of community and growth in the life of God's servants?
options: It shows the need for adequate space to grow in ministry
It teaches isolation as preferable for spiritual growth
It discourages expansion of prophetic groups
It prioritizes material wealth over community
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the need for adequate space to grow in ministry
questions.explanation: Verses 1-2 display the sons of the prophets desiring more room to dwell and minister, highlighting communal growth and provision for God's work (Acts 2:44-46).

questions.question: By combining 2 Kings 6:15-17 and 2 Kings 6:21-22, what theological truth about divine protection and human response is taught?
options: God's protection is assured but requires faith and mercy from His people
God protects but humans must fight fiercely without mercy
God's protection is limited to physical safety only
questions.correctAnswer: God's protection is assured but requires faith and mercy from His people
questions.explanation: Verses 15-17 show God’s unseen protection, and 21-22 reveal the king’s merciful treatment of captives, teaching that divine protection coincides with faith and mercy (Psalm 91:1-4).

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by Elisha's confident declaration in 2 Kings 6:16 that 'they that be with us are more than they that be with them'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence
questions.explanation: Verse 16 reflects Elisha’s faith in God's omnipotence, affirming God's superior power despite physical odds (Jeremiah 32:17).

questions.question: Which doctrine is underscored by the famine's severity described in 2 Kings 6:25, where even an ass's head is sold for eighty pieces of silver?
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine judgment
questions.explanation: The extreme famine in 6:25 symbolizes God's judgment on Israel for their sins, a common biblical theme (Leviticus 26:21-22).

questions.question: How does the interaction between the king of Israel and the woman in 2 Kings 6:26-30 reveal the human condition in relation to divine deliverance?
options: It reveals desperation and the need for God's intervention
It shows humans can always save themselves
It indicates that suffering is unrelated to sin
It portrays hope in political solutions only
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals desperation and the need for God's intervention
questions.explanation: These verses depict extreme human suffering and helplessness, emphasizing reliance on God for deliverance (Psalm 107:6).

questions.question: What combined theological lesson is conveyed by 2 Kings 6:8-10 and 2 Kings 6:12-13 about the role of prophecy and God's protection?
options: Prophets reveal God's protective knowledge over His people
Prophecy is unreliable in times of war
God does not intervene in political affairs
Kings act independently of God's will
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets reveal God's protective knowledge over His people
questions.explanation: Verses 8-10 show Elisha warning the king of Israel about enemy plans, and 12-13 reveal the Syrians' frustration at his prophetic insight, affirming prophecy as a means of divine protection (1 Samuel 9:9).

questions.question: What does the reaction of the king of Israel in 2 Kings 6:31-32 teach about leadership in times of divine crisis?
options: Faithful leaders uphold and protect God's prophets
Leaders should abandon prophetic counsel quickly
Leadership is primarily political without spiritual concern
Leaders must rely only on military strength
questions.correctAnswer: Faithful leaders uphold and protect God's prophets
questions.explanation: The king vows to protect Elisha's life despite threats (6:31-32), showing that godly leadership honors and supports prophetic ministry (1 Kings 19:18).
